$comment: England & Wales, Pensions Law - the interpretive principles for construing pension scheme trust deeds and rules, and the RPI-to-CPI indexation dispute that produced them. Fresh research this session. Both nodes are post-2016/2018 and fetched directly, no BAILII/pre-2009 access issue to route around.

authorities.name: Barnardo's v Buckinghamshire and others
authorities.judge_or_panel: Lord Hodge (sole judgment; Lady Hale, Lord Wilson, Lord Sumption, Lord Briggs agreeing)
authorities.proposition: Sets out, for the first time in a Supreme Court decision, general principles for construing pension scheme trust deeds and rules: such instruments are formal, professionally drafted, not the product of bilateral commercial negotiation, designed to operate over the long term, and relied on by non-drafting parties (the members) - so courts should give more weight to textual analysis and less to background factual matrix than in an ordinary commercial contract construed under the Rainy Sky/Arnold v Britton/Wood v Capita trilogy. On the facts, under the 1988 Barnardo's scheme rules the trustees had no power to switch the indexation measure from RPI to CPI merely because they judged CPI a better measure - the power to select a different index arose only if RPI itself ceased to be published or was officially replaced. Appeal dismissed.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on paragraph 15's textual-analysis principle. Cross-checked against the UK Supreme Court's own case page. BAILII's copy was blocked by an anti-scraping challenge and was not used - not needed, since Find Case Law covers this post-2009 case directly.

authorities.name: Barnardo's and others v Buckinghamshire and others (Court of Appeal)
authorities.judge_or_panel: Sir Geoffrey Vos, Chancellor (dissenting); McFarlane LJ, Lewison LJ (majority)
authorities.proposition: By a 2-1 majority, upheld the first-instance ruling that the trustees had no rule-making power to substitute CPI for RPI while RPI remained a published index. The Chancellor dissented, construing the scheme's 'General Index' definition as permitting trustee discretion to adopt a different index. This decision was the one under appeal to, and affirmed by, the Supreme Court in Barnardo's v Buckinghamshire [2018] UKSC 55 above.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering pension scheme rule construction and the specific RPI/CPI indexation dispute that produced the leading principles. Does not cover trustee fiduciary duties generally, the Pension Protection Fund's role, automatic enrolment, or any other Pensions Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
